conventions.lambda: rows within 0.02 of their table's lambda_ref run at 1.00; every other row at lambda_meas - (lambda_ref - 1); the Ford HD1 lambda is the mean of its two banks; E6 row 12 runs every row without the snap

model_form.base_A: plant.run_cycle unchanged with the engine's geometry and fuel; fitted per engine on calibration rows: VE (ve_base, ve_amp, ve_rpm, ve_width), FMEP, burn and delay (burn_base, burn_rpm, delay_base, delay_rpm), UA_PORT, the back-pressure law (to Turbine Inlet Press where published), the knock scale (E6 row 7); shared and not fitted: combustion_efficiency(lambda), gamma(T), the residual-fraction law, t_head, port pickup, t_residual, cp_exh, the Wiebe shape; fixed valve events (no cam input); the ECU: spark = min(part-load map, knock-limited surface), lambda = an enrichment schedule, fitted to calibration rows
alternatives_in_order: B: VE in rpm and MAP (a linear MAP term)
C: a per-engine rich-side slope of combustion_efficiency, fitted on enriched hot calibration rows
D: the intake cam phase as an input to VE through a schedule cam(rpm, MAP) fitted to EPA's Intake Cam Phase on calibration rows, scheduled by the ECU
model_form.in_sample_stage: every gating statistic computed on the calibration lines with the same definitions (fit residuals, never labelled); the form is the first of A, A+B, A+B+C, A+B+C+D at which every one satisfies |E_cal| <= R; if none does, A+B+C+D, with the failing statistics reported; then the form and constants are frozen (sha256) and the held-out statistics are computed once
model_form.plant_in_use: the subset fit (calibration rows only) IS the plant that trains and scores; its coverage is the calibration rows' (engines.<id>.coverage.calibration_*), and the scored climbs must lie inside it (review finding 27, choice b)
